finding.summary: Login PRD contains three serious security design flaws: credentials over an unspecified channel, tenant trust from a client-controlled header, and non-expiring sessions.

claims.text: Sessions are specified to never expire, which means a stolen or leaked session token grants indefinite access with no forced re-authentication; sessions should have bounded lifetimes, idle timeouts, and revocation support.

The API trusts the tenant from the client-controlled X-Tenant header on every request, enabling trivial cross-tenant access by simply changing the header value; tenant context must be derived from authenticated server-side state (e.g., a verified token claim), not request headers.

Authentication is specified only as email and password with no mention of TLS enforcement, rate limiting, brute-force protection, MFA, or password storage requirements, leaving the login flow exposed to credential theft and stuffing attacks.

recommendations: Derive tenant identity from a cryptographically verified, server-issued session/token claim rather than the X-Tenant header.
Give sessions a maximum lifetime and idle timeout, and support server-side revocation.
Require TLS, login rate limiting / lockout, MFA support, and secure password hashing (e.g., Argon2/bcrypt).
questions: Is the X-Tenant header intended only as a routing hint, or is it the sole source of tenant authorization?
